solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leader of Tories in posh headgear? Well I never!

indicators.note: the leading letter sits inside the hat phrase, so in signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: a fancy hat is smart, elaborate headwear

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here taken from Tories

explanation.surface: A Conservative boss turns up in an extravagant hat, and an onlooker gasps in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' splits the headgear phrase to admit the Tory leader; the hat is not the definition, the exclamation at the end is.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of mild astonishment, used interchangeably in everyday speech.

clue.text: Result of putting lots of dough in the kitty?

definitions.text: Result of putting lots of dough in the kitty?

parts.words: Result of putting lots of dough in the kitty?
parts.note: read literally, overfeeding a pet cat makes it plump; read as slang, dough is money and a kitty a fund, so a person loaded with cash

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what happens when you stuff a pet with food, or a money pot with cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy, privileged person is slangily called this; a cat fed too much bread would also literally fit.

indicators.note: the answer slips covertly into the words town in Japan, spanning them like an agent

explanation.surface: A killer sneaks into a Japanese town, which suits the warrior on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: These covert Japanese agents were hired for espionage and killing, so a trained assassin.

indicators.note: the department word is placed within the word for a minor

parts.note: a minor is a young person, a youth
an arm is a branch or department of an organisation

explanation.surface: A government department is housed in some small coastal resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' looks like an adjective for the seaside town but is the noun YOUTH. Great Yarmouth is a resort on the Norfolk coast in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a port and holiday resort on the east coast of England, as well as one in Nova Scotia.

indicators.note: flying here means the letters of our helicopter take wing and rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: A sleuth piloting the aircraft we own.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's Belgian private investigator is one of fiction's best-known sleuths.

clue.text: Got up, put on a white robe

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one piece on another places it above, so it comes first
in a down clue, up means the word Got is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Someone rose and dressed in a pale gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up' looks like rising from bed; it is GOT reversed, TOG, which 'put on' sets above A.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment worn by Roman citizens was traditionally a draped, plain white woollen cloak.

clue.text: Gangster loses one item of clothing

indicators.note: the gangster's name loses the word one, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster mislays a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' removes ONE, spelt out, from the end of CAPONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A peaked or brimless piece of headwear counts as an item someone wears.

definitions.meaning: to grow bacteria or cells in a lab medium is this verb
a society's arts, customs and achievements

explanation.surface: A slogan about fostering the advancement of society.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists grow cells in a dish under this verb; as a noun it means a people's arts and way of life.

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
ET is the film's extraterrestrial, a crossword alien

explanation.surface: A plot hatched together with an extraterrestrial planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A world is any celestial body like Mars or Earth orbiting a star.

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters of note are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A musical put-down: one bum note, but the vocalist is the correct one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' tempts as the musical clue for the singer, but it is anagram fodder, made TENO by 'Wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the high male voice part, so one who sings it.

indicators.note: a destroyed word is broken up, so the letters of Algeria are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A North African country wrecks the emblems of monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowns, sceptres and orbs are the ceremonial emblems carried or worn by a monarch.

clue.text: Girl with record, we hear, that's something comparable

indicators.note: we hear signals that what follows is said aloud, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name and a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A young woman with her diary turns out to be a close parallel.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a thing with a counterpart or parallel, closely similar in function to another.

indicators.note: a beheaded word has its head, the opening letter, cut off

parts.note: a prude is a puritan, easily shocked

explanation.surface: A coarse prig is executed.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude or impolite language is described as vulgar, offensive to good taste.

definitions.meaning: an offence in football of touching the ball with the arm
a team sport where the ball is struck or thrown by hand

explanation.surface: A rotten sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: In football an infringement for touching the ball with the arm; it is also an Olympic court sport played with the hands.

indicators.note: restored suggests the letters of meander to are rebuilt into a new form

explanation.surface: Wander along to a renovated great church.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the fire-damaged Paris cathedral being restored, which disguises 'restored' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Gothic church on the Île de la Cité in Paris is a cathedral.

indicators.note: reused letters are put to work again in a fresh arrangement, so vet only is rearranged

explanation.surface: A recycled thing from the animal doctor turns out to be fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh, unusual thing or the quality of newness is so called.

indicators.note: invention here means creative reworking, so is done is rearranged

explanation.surface: An inventor finishes by inventing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American who devised the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Aid for smoking, herring primarily having gone missing

indicators.note: the first letter of herring having gone means it is removed

parts.note: an ashtray is a dish a smoker uses for ash

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of herring

explanation.surface: A smoker's accessory and a smoked fish have both vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gone' removes H, the first letter of herring, from ASHTRAY. 'missing' at the end looks part of the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray is lost or mislaid, so absent from where it should be.

indicators.note: bringing back the word means turning it round, read from the end

parts.note: avid means keen, enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A plea to reinstate an eager soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated female opera star, a prima donna, is called this.

clue.text: Leaders of drinking society drink vintage liquor for melancholy

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so the two leading letters take the other pieces inside them
leaders are the opening letters of drinking and society

parts.note: vintage means old
rum is a spirit, a liquor

explanation.surface: The heads of a drinking club down aged spirits to cure their gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' looks like part of the boozy surface but is the containment signal: the two leading letters swallow the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doldrums is an idiom for low spirits and gloomy inactivity.

parts.note: un is French for a
a tie is a match in a cup competition

explanation.surface: A French contest held apart from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a cup tie is a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: To unknot or unfasten things is to separate them, as a verb.

parts.note: to rig is to fix fraudulently, as a vote

explanation.surface: Fraud in some city on the Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital of Latvia, on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Service person putting iodine in join

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places the iodine symbol inside
in completes the instruction to set the letter within the join word

parts.note: to solder is to join metals
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A military man doing some metalwork with a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an armed service, especially the army, is one.

clue.text: Starts to acquire cheap tops off rugby player

indicators.note: the starts of these five words are their first letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: A rugby player goes about buying cut-price shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rugby player' wants to read as one sporting phrase; 'rugby' is fodder and 'player' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone performing a part on stage, a thespian.

clue.text: Sneaky on a regular basis? No!

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means every other letter of sneaky

explanation.surface: Asking if someone is regularly devious, and getting a flat denial.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned or formal word for a negative vote or denial.

clue.text: Big guns badly stuck in main road

indicators.note: stuck in means one piece is jammed inside the other

parts.note: an artery is a main road
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Heavy weaponry has broken down in the middle of a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big guns' could be important people, but here means heavy weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Large mounted firearms such as cannon are collectively called this.
